transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up time someone else might need more. 

My family actually suggested I come in, just because I've been a little... stressed, I guess you could say? It's regarding my father's passing. I know everyone keeps telling me that the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly, and I really do try to listen to them. I don't want to be difficult. But... well, I work with data for a living, so I notice small discrepancies. When I compare the timestamps and notice missing attachments... and then see the way certain community members just sort of avoid my questions... it’s just obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I don't want to cause any trouble, I really don't, but the details just don't match up. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining this okay.
Do you believe that others are actively hiding information about your father's death from you?

Well... yes, I suppose I do. I mean, I really hope I'm not sounding paranoid or—or like I'm accusing anyone of something terrible. I know that probably sounds bad. But it's just... like I said, when I look at the hospital records and the donation emails, everyone tells me they line up perfectly. And I want to believe them, I really do. 

But then I see the timestamps that don't quite match, and the missing attachments in the emails... and when I try to just politely ask a few people in the community about it, they just sort of change the subject or avoid me entirely. It's just... it feels obvious to me that something is being kept from me about how he died. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds like a lot. Does that seem completely unreasonable to you? I really value your professional opinion on this.
For how long have you been thinking that someone is hiding information about your father's death from you?

Well, um... I guess it's been about nine months now. It started right after he passed away, when I was, you know, just trying to be helpful and sort through all his records and his old messages. 

I really didn't mean to go looking for anything out of the ordinary. I was just trying to get his affairs in order, like any good son would do, right? But that's when I started noticing the little things that didn't add up. So... yeah, about nine months. I hope I haven't been obsessing over it too much... does nine months seem like a long time to still be looking into this?
Do you think that the community members who avoid your questions are specifically trying to hide something from you, or is it more that they are just not willing to talk about it?

Well, um... I guess it's a bit of both? I mean, I know death makes people uncomfortable, and I really try not to be pushy. I hate making people feel awkward. But... it's just, when you look at the whole picture—the missing attachments, the timestamps that are just slightly off... it's hard not to feel like the avoidance is part of it. 

Like I said, I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. And I don't want to think badly of anyone in the community, I really don't. But when I try to ask just basic, polite questions to clarify things, and they won't even look me in the eye... it just feels so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm repeating myself. I just... I want to be reasonable about this. Does it sound like I'm reading too much into their reactions? I'd really appreciate your thoughts on it.
Do you believe that the community members' avoidance of your questions is specifically about you and your father's death, or is it just their general discomfort with discussing death?

Um... I really wish I could just chalk it up to general discomfort. That would be so much easier, and I really don't want to be a burden or make things difficult for anyone. But... well, it feels very specific to him. 

I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly, and I promise I'm trying to listen to them. I don't want to be unreasonable. But when I actually sit down and compare the timestamps, and I see those missing attachments... and then I combine that with the way certain community members completely avoid my questions... it's just, it's obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around my father's death. 

I'm so sorry, I know I sound like a broken record today, and I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult or paranoid. Do you think it's possible I'm just analyzing the data too closely because of my background in IT, or... or does it make sense to you why I'd come to that conclusion?
If someone could provide you with conclusive evidence that there was no foul play involved in your father's death, would that change your beliefs about what happened?

Um... I would really like to say yes. I mean, I want to be the kind of person who just accepts the proof and moves on, I really do. I don't want to be difficult about this. 

But... well, I know I keep bringing this up, and I'm sorry to repeat myself again, but everyone already tells me they have the evidence. They keep saying the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly. But... when I look at the data myself, with the mismatched timestamps and the missing attachments... and then I see how those community members just completely shut down and avoid me... 

It's just... to me, it already feels so obviously clear that someone is hiding the truth about what happened to him. I feel like I'm looking right at the proof of a cover-up, you know? I can't just unsee it, even when people tell me everything is fine. 

I'm really trying to keep an open mind, I promise. Does that make me sound too stubborn? I really hope you don't think I'm just ignoring reason... I just want to do right by my dad.
Do you think your belief that someone is hiding information about your father's death could be wrong?

I mean... I really want to be open to that possibility. I know how important it is to stay objective, and I'm really trying not to be rigid about this. I'd hate for you to think I'm just completely closed off to logic. 

But... it's just so hard to shake. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly, and I really do hear them. But when I look at those timestamps, and the missing attachments... and then the way people in the community just avoid me when I ask... I don't know, it just feels so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm saying the exact same thing again. I just... I can't seem to look past it, even though I know it probably sounds like I'm not listening to reason. Do you think I'm being too stubborn about this? I really am trying to look at it from all sides...
How would you feel if you were to discover that your beliefs about your father's death were incorrect?

Um... wow, I... I honestly don't know. I haven't really let myself think about it like that. 

I guess... I mean, I'd like to think I would be relieved? It would certainly make things a lot easier for everyone else, and I really, really don't want to be a burden on the community or... or on you, taking up your time with all this. If I was wrong, it would mean I could just stop causing so much trouble and let everyone move on. 

But... yeah, I just don't have a clear answer for how I'd actually process it inside. I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not a very helpful response. Is it okay that I don't really know how to answer that? I really hope I'm still giving you what you need for your assessment... I'm trying my best to be cooperative.
How would you feel emotionally if you were to discover that your beliefs about your father's death were completely incorrect?

Um... emotionally? Wow. I... I really don't know. 

I guess I tend to look at things so analytically, you know, with my background in systems and data, that I haven't really unpacked the emotional side of it at all. I mean, I'd probably feel pretty embarrassed? Like I made a big fuss over nothing and wasted your time, which is the absolute last thing I want to do. 

But deep down, like, true emotions... I just haven't let myself go there. I'm sorry, I know you're trying to get a complete picture of my mental state and I'm probably not giving you very much to work with. Is it alright that I don't really have a good answer for that part? I really hope I'm not being too difficult to assess.
Do you think your belief about your father's death is based on facts or is it just a feeling you have?

Um... I really want to say it's based on facts. With my background as a systems analyst, I always try to rely on actual data, not just... feelings. I know I brought some of this up a few minutes ago, and I'm really sorry to sound like a broken record—I hope I'm not being too repetitive for your notes. 

But to me, they really do feel like facts. Like I mentioned, I know everyone insists the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly. But when I actually sit down and compare the data... the timestamps that don't match, the attachments that are clearly missing from the threads... and then you add in the observable way certain people in the community physically avoid my questions... 

I don't know, to me, those are concrete things, not just emotions. It just makes it so obvious that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. It's not just a gut feeling, it's... it's right there in the discrepancies. 

Does that make sense? I really hope I'm explaining my thought process clearly enough for you. I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.

Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would change if everyone in the community, including the hospital staff, provided a unified and consistent explanation for the discrepancies you've found?

Oh, wow. Um... that's a really good question. I... I want to say yes? I really, really want to be reasonable about all this. It would be so much easier if I could just accept what everyone is saying and put it to rest. 

But... well, I know I just mentioned this, and I'm so sorry if I'm going in circles, but... even if they all suddenly came to me with one perfectly consistent story today, I still have the original data. Like I was saying before, everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the emails line up perfectly, but I've already seen the mismatched timestamps and the missing attachments. And... I've already experienced the way certain people avoid my questions. 

So, if they suddenly had a unified explanation now... I think a part of me would just wonder if they finally coordinated their stories to hide what really happened to him. 

I'm sorry, does that make me sound incredibly stubborn? I promise I'm not trying to be difficult or dismissive of your question. I'm really trying to keep an open mind. I just... I can't unsee the discrepancies, you know? I really hope I'm still being helpful for your assessment, I just want to be as honest with you as possible.
Do you think it's possible that your interpretation of the data is incorrect, even if it seems convincing to you?

Um... I mean, I really want to say yes. I know that's probably the answer I *should* give, right? With my background, I know that human error is always a factor in any analysis, so technically, yes, it's possible my interpretation could be wrong. I really, really hope I am wrong, honestly. That would be a huge relief. 

It's just... well, I know I've already talked your ear off about this, and I'm so sorry to keep bringing the same things up. I really don't want to be a nuisance or seem like I'm not listening to reason. But when everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly, and then I actually look at them and see the missing attachments, the timestamps being off... and then I see the way certain people in the community just completely avoid looking me in the eye when I ask about it... 

It just makes it so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. Even though I want to admit I could be wrong, the things I'm seeing just keep pointing me back to that same conclusion. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably not the best answer, and I really hope I'm not coming across as too difficult or defensive. Am I making any sense at all? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need for your evaluation. Is that an okay answer?
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death would change if you were shown conclusive, irrefutable evidence that contradicted them?

Um... conclusive, irrefutable evidence... I mean, yes. Yes, of course. I really, really want to be the kind of person who can look at hard proof and change my mind. I try very hard to be logical, and I would honestly love to just... let it all go. It would be wonderful if you could show me something that just cleared it all up. 

But... oh gosh, I know I keep saying this, and I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just wasting your time repeating myself. I just... I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly. They all say it's fine. But when I sit there and I look at the timestamps that don't match, and the missing attachments... and then I see the way certain community members just physically avoid my questions... 

It's just so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. So, if someone showed me new evidence... I guess I would just be really worried that it was manufactured? Or manipulated somehow to cover up the discrepancies I've already found. 

I'm so sorry, does that make me sound completely unreasonable? I promise I'm not trying to be difficult, I just... I want to make sure I'm giving you the most honest answer I can. Is it okay that I feel that way? I hope I'm still doing this right.
Do you feel like you could ever stop thinking about the discrepancies in your father's death records?

Um... stop thinking about it? I... I really want to say yes. I would love nothing more than to just turn my brain off and move on. I know it probably seems like I'm obsessed, and I really don't want to come across that way. I try so hard to focus on my work and my daily life, I really do. 

It's just... well, I know I've brought this up a few times already, and I'm so sorry to keep circling back to it. I know you're probably tired of hearing about it. But when I try to put it out of my mind, I just keep remembering how everyone insists the hospital records and those donation emails line up perfectly. And then I remember the mismatched timestamps I found, and those missing attachments. And the way those people in the community just... look away when I try to talk to them. 

It just makes it so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death, you know? And when you see something like that... it's just really hard to unsee it, even when you want to. 

I'm sorry, I know I should probably just let it go. Does that make me sound completely neurotic? I really hope I'm not being too frustrating to talk to. I just want to make sure I'm giving you a clear picture of where my head is at. Is that a helpful answer for your notes?
Would anything be able to change your mind about what happened to your father?

Um... change my mind? I... I really wish I could give you a simple yes. I know that's what a reasonable person would say, and I try so hard to be reasonable. I really don't want to be difficult or seem like I'm completely closed off. 

But... oh, I know I'm sounding like a broken record again, and I'm so incredibly sorry to keep harping on the exact same things. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly. They keep saying there's nothing to see. But when I actually sit down and compare those mismatched timestamps, and the missing attachments... and then I see how certain community members just completely avoid my questions or look the other way when I bring it up... 

It just makes it so overwhelmingly obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. So... I guess, to honestly answer your question... it would be really hard for anything to change my mind at this point, because I feel like I've already seen what's really going on. 

I'm sorry, I know that makes me sound so incredibly stubborn, and I promise I'm usually not like this at all. I hope you're not upset with me for saying that. Does that make sense, though, from my perspective? Am I still answering your questions okay?
Do you think you will ever be able to accept that your father's death was due to natural causes, without any foul play involved?

Um... natural causes. I... I really, really want to be able to say yes to that. I know it would make everything so much easier for my family, and probably for you, too. I really hate being the person who can't just accept things and move on. I want to be agreeable, I really do.

But... oh, I'm so embarrassed to keep bringing this up, because I know I've already mentioned it, and I really don't want to sound like a broken record. I know everyone, absolutely everyone, keeps telling me that the hospital records and those donation emails all line up perfectly. They say it was just a normal, natural death and there's nothing to see. But... well, as an analyst, my brain is just wired to look at data, you know? And when I sit down and compare those timestamps, and the missing attachments... and then I combine that with the way certain community members just completely avoid my questions... 

I'm sorry, I know I've said it a hundred times, but it's just so obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. So... accepting that there was no foul play... I just don't know how I could do that without feeling like I'm ignoring the facts right in front of me. 

I'm really sorry, I know that's not the answer you're hoping for. Am I making things too difficult? I promise I'm trying my best to work with you on this. Is it okay that I'm just being honest about how it looks to me? I really hope I'm not being a bad patient.
Do you think your beliefs about your father's death are affecting your daily life or relationships?

Um... affecting my life? I... I really want to say no, not at all. I try so incredibly hard to keep everything perfectly normal, because I really don't want this to become a burden on anyone, and I definitely don't want you to think I'm falling apart. I pride myself on being responsible, I really do. 

I still go to work every day, I'm handling all my systems analysis projects without any issues, I pay my bills on time, and I keep up with my normal routine. I promise I'm keeping everything together on that front. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm letting my life derail, because I'm really trying my best to stay on top of things.

I guess... well, to be completely transparent with you, because I know you need the whole picture to do your job... the main place things get a little, um, tense... is just when I try to bring up my questions about my father's records with my family, or with some of the community members. 

They get a little upset or shut down, and I absolutely hate causing any friction. I really do. I know it's probably so frustrating for them to hear me talk about it, and I feel terrible for making them uncomfortable. But aside from those specific conversations, I really am functioning just fine. 

Is... is that okay? I hope that shows I'm still doing reasonably well and not letting this take over completely. Does that answer your question the way you needed?
Do you think it's possible that your perception of the discrepancies in your father's death records is not based on reality?

Um... not based on reality? I... I really want to be open to everything you're suggesting. I know you're the expert here, and I completely respect your perspective. I really don't want to come across as someone who just flat-out rejects professional advice, because I try so hard to be self-aware and reasonable. 

And I know, I really do know, that everyone—my family, the hospital, everyone—keeps telling me that those records and the donation emails all line up perfectly. I know they all think I'm just seeing things that aren't there. And part of me really wishes they were right, because it would make all of this so much simpler for everyone involved. I hate being the one causing a fuss.

But... oh, I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm just repeating myself and being difficult, and I really don't want to be. It's just... when I actually sit down, with my analyst background, and I look at those mismatched timestamps... and the attachments that are clearly missing... and then I see the way certain community members physically turn away or change the subject when I try to ask about it... 

It just feels so incredibly real and obvious to me that someone is hiding the truth about his death. So... I guess, to answer your question honestly, it's really hard for me to see it as not based on reality, because the data is right there in front of me. 

I'm so sorry if that's frustrating to hear. I promise I'm not trying to be combative or difficult. I really value your help. Does that make sense, though? Am I being too stubborn about this? I hope you're not disappointed in me for saying that.
Do you think it's possible that your beliefs about your father's death are a product of your own mind, rather than based on actual events?

Um... a product of my own mind? I... I really want to give you the answer you're looking for, I truly do. I know you're just trying to help me, and I appreciate that so much. I hate the idea that I might be wasting your time or being a difficult case. I really try to be objective about myself.

And I know... I know I've said this before, and I'm so embarrassed to keep bringing it up, but... I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and those donation emails all line up. I know they all think I'm just making this up in my head, and I really, really wish I could just agree with them and with you. It would be so much easier if it was just my imagination.

But... well, when I look at the actual data... the timestamps that don't match, and those attachments that are just... missing... and then I see how certain people in the community completely avoid me when I ask even the simplest questions... it just... it feels so incredibly obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds like I'm just rejecting what you're saying, and I promise I'm not trying to be stubborn. It's just... the details are right there, you know? I... I hope that's okay to say. Am I being too difficult? I really want to be a good patient and work through this with you.
